en: When we created our meeting prep file, we
described a step-by-step process which we
used once here.
But of course, in a normal work environment,
this could be reused because we could use
this logic for any meeting you might have
every day, every week,
whenever you want. And then we would have to
describe all these steps again and again and
again. So we have to describe that we have a
meeting,
that we want
Claude to check our calendar, our emails,
and our files.
And then it should create a.docx file with
the details, the agenda, the key talking
points, and so on.
Whenever we have such a process, such a
repetitive step-by-step task in the end,
we can use so-called skills.
By skills, you can add a set of instructions
that teaches Claude how to do a specific
task the same way every time.
And we used skills already here in our
project.
When we
created the.docx file, or when Cowork
created that.docx file,
it used the docx skill.
This is a built-in skill that ships with
Cowork. You generally don't need to edit it
and Anthropic maintains it so CoVer can
reliably create Word documents.
You can still inspect built-in skills the
same way you inspect personal ones, but
treat them as system skills.
Leave them as they are unless you have a
very specific reason to change them.
You can see some more skills which are
already implemented though.
In our Customize menu,
in the Create New Skills section,
we can find some skills too.
At the top, we have personal skills. These
are skills added by the Anthropic team,
which we'll explore in a few seconds.
And you can find some built-in skills. These
skills are required to use features like
scheduling tasks, which we'll also explore
in this course. So when we schedule tasks,
this built-in skill will be used
automatically.
The personal skill here at the top is a bit
more interesting though, because in this
area we can view
the existing personal skills,
we can activate or deactivate these,
we can also uninstall skills,
and we can also view or edit the actual
content of that skill, so the actual
goal of that skill.
Now, this skill is a skill which is added by
the Anthropic team, which allows Claude to
create, modify, or improve existing skills.
And at the top here, we have the skill
description.
This description is very important because
whenever you're writing a task in Claude
Cowork, based on the content of this task,
Claude will scan the description of your
current skills And if a description matches
the task, it will further investigate if
this skill is required for the task it has
to fulfill now.
So for example, if I tell Claude to create a
new skill, it will scan the description here
and find out that this skill is required to
create a new skill.
Now I won't dive into the skill in a lot of
detail.
It is
added by Anthropic and it's very detailed.
This skill also contains a skill markdown
file which is the file we just viewed, which
is the actual core content, but it also
contains more subfolders for agents, for
assets, for further scripts, and so on. So
that's a quite complex skill containing lots
of scripts
and MD files and folders. And if we go back
to our example, we could add a skill on our
own now for this process that lets us
generate our meeting notes.
